summary:
[  edit  ]
The Timecode  CHOP  generates  Timecode  data (channels, a  .timecode  python object and other python members). Its Mode menu provides a variety of ways to get, set and generate timecode through its parameters, including being driven from a timecode string, a set of channels, or other OPs that have timecode such as video input devices. You can also set timecode with python functions.
The timecode data is output as both channel data in the  CHOP , and as a  Timecode object  via its   .timecode  member  in Python.
The timecode can follow the SMPTE standard (ie. non-negative, frames-per-second up to 60, loops at 24 hours), or a more general format (ie. any number of frames per second, negative timecode allowed, loops at 100 hours).
When being driven by channels, an input with channels named  negative ,  hour ,  minute ,  second , or  frame  can be provided that is added to the Timecode  CHOP 's output.
See also:  Timecode ,  Timecode Class  and the OP  Snippets  for the Timecode  CHOP .

inputs.description: - Optional input  CHOP  with some or all of following channels: negative, hour, minute, second, frame. The input timecode value is added to the Timecode  CHOP 's output.

parameters.label: SMPTE
parameters.name: smpte
parameters.description: When enabled the generated timecode will follow the  SMPTE timecode  standard, meaning no negative timecodes, and the timecode will loop at 24 hours. When disabled, the format will be more general, allowing for negative numbers and a maximum timecode of 100 hours.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: ⊞  - The source used for generating the timecode

parameters.label: Locked to  Timeline
parameters.name: lockedtotimeline
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from the timeline's time.

parameters.label: Specify Index
parameters.name: specifyindex
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from a single index value.

parameters.label: Timecode String
parameters.name: timecodestr
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from a timecode string following the format:  hh:mm:ss:ff  or  hh:mm:ss.ff

parameters.label: Hour, Minute, Second, Frame Parameters
parameters.name: timecodepar
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from hour, minute, second, and frame parameters. The parameters will overflow from one to the next, eg. specifying 120 seconds will output timecode as  00:02:00:00 . Fractional values are also allowed.

parameters.label: Sequential
parameters.name: sequential
parameters.description: The timecode increases sequentially over time.

parameters.label: Timecode  Object
parameters.name: timecodeobj
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from a  timecode object .

parameters.label: CHOP  Channels
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from a  CHOP  reference with some or all of the channels: negative, hour, minute, second, frame.

parameters.label: OP  Reference
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: Generates the timecode from an OP with a timecode Python member, eg.  MoviefileinTOP_Class .

parameters.label: Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: The timecode  FPS . The timecode's max frame value is equal to  rate-1 . If a fractional rate is provided then the rate is rounded up to the nearest whole number and drop-frames will be calculated if enabled on the Drop Frame parameter.

parameters.label: Drop  Frame
parameters.name: dropframe
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify how to calculate  drop-frames . Drop frames are used when the  FPS  is fractional.  FPS  cannot increment a fractional amount per frame so  FPS  is rounded to the next whole number and the accumulation of error is accommodated for by adding drop frames.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Drop-frames will not added.

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: auto
parameters.description: Drop-frames will be added to the timecode when the rate is fractional. For special rate values such as 29.97, the defined standard solution is used (ie. 2 frames added every minute, except minutes that are divisible by 10). In other cases, a general solution is used by calculating the accumulated error.

parameters.label: Index
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index used to generate the timecode. Value is used in conjunction with the specified units.

parameters.label: Index Unit
parameters.name: indexunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - The index value units.

parameters.label: Timecode String
parameters.name: timecodestr
parameters.description: A timecode string following the format:  hh:mm:ss:ff  or  hh:mm:ss.ff

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: Frame component of the timecode.

parameters.label: Second
parameters.name: second
parameters.description: Second component of the timecode.

parameters.label: Minute
parameters.name: minute
parameters.description: Minute component of the timecode. Allows for overflow.

parameters.label: Hour
parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: Hour component of the timecode.

parameters.label: Initialize
parameters.name: init
parameters.description: Used in sequential mode. Initializes the timecode value.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Used in sequential mode. Starts the timecode sequential increment.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: When enabled, the sequential timecode will step forward.

parameters.label: Timecode  Object
parameters.name: timecodeobj
parameters.description: A  timecode object .

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: A  CHOP  reference which contains some or all of the following channels: negative, hour, minute, second, frame.

parameters.label: OP
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: An OP reference that contains a timecode Python member: eg.  MoviefileinTOP_Class .

parameters.label: Custom Length
parameters.name: customlength
parameters.description: ⊞  - If set to "By Value", then the Length parameter is used. If set to "By Timecode", then the Length Timecode Object is used. If set to "Off", then the default length will be 23:59:59:ff-1 for a SMPTE timecode and 99:59:59:ff-1 otherwise.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: When selected, will not use a custom length. The length will default to 23:59:59:ff-1 for a SMPTE timecode and 99:59:59:ff-1 otherwise.

parameters.label: By Value
parameters.name: value
parameters.description: When selected, set the custom length from a value using the Length parameter.

parameters.label: By Timecode  Object
parameters.name: timecodeobj
parameters.description: When selected, set the custom length from a  timecode object  using the Length Timecode Object parameter.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Specifies the custom length in either samples, frames, or seconds.

parameters.label: Length Units
parameters.name: lengthunits
parameters.description: ⊞  - The unit of the custom length.

parameters.label: Length Timecode  Object
parameters.name: lengthtimecodeobj
parameters.description: Specifies the custom length as a  timecode object .

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: extendleft
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the timecode behavior when exceeding the lower bound of 00:00:00:00 for SMPTE timecode and -99:59:59:ff+1 otherwise.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: If selected, then the timecode will hold its value when exceeding lower bound: 00:00:00:00 for SMPTE timecode and -99:59:59:ff+1 otherwise.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: If selected, then the timecode will cycle its value when exceeding lower bound. It will cycle to the length value for SMPTE timecode and 00:00:00:00 otherwise.

parameters.label: Extend Right
parameters.name: extendright
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the timecode behavior when exceeding the upper bound defined by the length parameters.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: If selected, then the timecode will hold its value to the length value.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: If selected, then the timecode will cycle to 00:00:00:00 once it reaches length.

parameters.label: Negative Chan
parameters.name: negativechan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the negative channel, which is true when the timecode is negative. Always false when using SMPTE standard.

parameters.label: Frame Chan
parameters.name: framechan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the frame channel.

parameters.label: Second Chan
parameters.name: secondchan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the second channel.

parameters.label: Minute Chan
parameters.name: minutechan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the minute channel.

parameters.label: Hour Chan
parameters.name: hourchan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the hour channel.

parameters.label: Total Seconds Chan
parameters.name: totalseconds
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the total_seconds channel, which is the timecode converted into seconds.

parameters.label: Total Frames Chan
parameters.name: totalframes
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the total_frames channel, which is the timecode into frames.

parameters.label: Drop Frame Chan
parameters.name: dropframechan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the drop_frame channel, which is true when the timecode is drop-frame.

parameters.label: FPS  Chan
parameters.name: fpschan
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs the fps channel.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
